title: System, Method, and Cryptographic Escrow Protocol for Bilateral Foreign Exchange Market-Making with Real-Time Performance Bond Escrows and Settlement-Evidence-Gated Release
description:
A formal systems engineering and cryptographic protocol technical disclosure establishing defensive prior art under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) and EPC Article 54(2) for an on-chain Foreign Exchange (FX) Market-Maker Performance Bond Escrow and Continuous Linked Settlement (CLS) clearing protocol.

Addressing the fundamental vulnerability of counterparty delivery default (Herstatt risk) in cross-border decentralized finance and Request-for-Quote (RFQ) markets—where liquidity makers stream uncollateralized quotes and can abandon execution during adverse price swings without economic penalty—this specification discloses a real-time, evidence-gated margin clearing protocol: (1) An authorized market maker must lock an immutable performance bond on an external ledger (e.g., XRP Ledger EscrowCreate) to an independent custodian prior to quote publication, embedding a domain-separated corridor linkage memo (X402M:corridor:maker); (2) An on-chain market contract (CorridorMarket.syn) records the quote on Layer-1 only upon registering the validated escrow transaction hash and sequence number, enabling downstream gateways to expose verified pricing metadata (margin_verified: true, fx_rate_source: 'market: '); (3) Collateral release is decoupled from time-locks (CancelAfter expiries) and third-party oracles, evaluating strictly on-chain ISO 20022 pacs.002 Acsc (Accepted Settlement Completed) payment status receipts anchored to consensus blocks; (4) Release requests referencing missing or unconfirmed settlement evidence fail closed (release_refused: evidence_missing); and (5) Upon verification of genuine settlement finality, the custodian executes an on-chain escrow finish transaction that atomically returns the locked margin in full to the maker and deletes the escrow object from the ledger state tree (escrow_gone=true).

The specification establishes mathematical and architectural symmetry between consumer API execution bonds and market-maker quotation margins, providing an institutional, collateralized foundation for bilateral agentic clearing across decentralized networks.
